1b9b7fc402575033: KOTA BARU: Kelantan Road Transport Department has detected a new tactic involving Myanmar citizens who legally enter the state but later provide Malaysian-registered vehicles to their Rohingya friends.
Kelantan RTD director Mohd Misuari Abdullah said the individuals would enter Malaysia legally with valid passports and permits before purchasing and registering vehicles in their names.
He said the vehicles, mostly motorcycles, would then be lent to Rohingya friends for their use and movement within the state.
"This is a new method that we have detected. They enter legally with valid permits and passports, buy and register vehicles in Malaysia, and later lend them to their Rohingya friends.
"Most of the vehicles involved are motorcycles," he told a press conference here today.
Misuari said the state RTD would work with other agencies to conduct integrated operations, particularly targeting vehicles believed to be used in such arrangements.
He believed curbing the use of such vehicles could help reduce the risk of criminal activities involving the community.
"If they use bicycles, that is not an issue for us.
"But when vehicles are involved, we need to monitor and take appropriate action," he said.
On another note, Misuari said some locals were still renting out vehicles to members of the community despite enforcement action against such practices.
He said several vehicle owners had been charged in court, resulting in fewer locals willing to rent out their vehicles.
"Some claim they did not know about the matter, while others say they felt sorry for Rohingya.
"However, we will continue monitoring this group and take appropriate action against those who violate the law," he said.
b4522253c095ff45: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — The Pokémon franchise turned 30 this year and for the first time Malaysia got to kick off a series of events in the region, namely the PokéXciting! Celebrations.
I spoke to Go Nagano, who is a director at The Pokémon Company, specialising in events, about PokeXciting!, its aims and what they thought of the response
A heartfelt thanks
Nagano said that as far as the event’s branding was concerned, ”We want to show our gratitude and appreciation to all the fans.”
He said that PokéXciting was planned to make it an enjoyable version for everyone—whether it was locals, tourists and of course, long-time Pokémon trainers.
That, Nagano, said, included people who only recently knew about Pokémon.

The PokéXciting! celebrations will have one final drone show tonight at 9pm. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
“How we planned this event, is like we wanted to make sure to embody our company’s mission statement, which is to enrich both the real world and the virtual world with the Pokémon characters.
“So we put together a lot of content for this event,” he said.
That included a stage show, parade and the in-game Pokémon Go experience.
First big Malaysian event
Nagano said that PokéXciting was the first time an event of such a scale was held in Malaysia.
He said it wouldn’t have been possible without local partners, especially the Petronas Group and KLCC.
“Thank you so much to our local partners,” he said, adding that they had been very supportive throughout the process.
Nagano said a lot of discussion went into specific content activation, figuring out what would appeal to local fans.
As to what he found most challenging and also what was most enjoyable about the whole endeavour, he said that the planning itself didn’t feel particularly hard.
“When we saw a lot of fans enjoying our event, we felt like it was a great reward for us.
“So to be honest, it didn’t feel really hard to get it prepared,” he said.
He said it was gratifying to see everyone really enjoying the prepared events such as the parade and stage show.
While they anticipated the good reception after the enthusiasm shown, it was still good to actually witness the numbers of people filling the park for PokéXciting.
Nagano said,”This is our first time bringing this scale of event to Malaysian fans so we really want everyone to enjoy it, and we believe this kind of event is very unique to Pokémon.”
One example of that was the very unique experience provided to Pokémon Go players, one he said that only the game could truly deliver.
As to whether Malaysians can look forward to more, Nagano laughed and would only say, “Keep enjoying the Pokémon.”
The second day of the PokéXciting! 30th anniversary of Pokémon celebrations will conclude today with a final drone show happening at 9pm.
The PokéXciting! celebrations will have one final drone show tonight at 9pm. — Picture by Raymond Manuel
6a0da5d29d2cef7e: KUALA LUMPUR: Glasgow Commonwealth Games champion Aniq Kasdan has skipped the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games to focus on his bid to qualify for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics.

Aniq is now preparing for the World Championships in Ningbo, China, from Oct 27-Nov 8, followed by the first International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) Olympic qualifier in Doha from Dec 7-16 as he begins his qualifying campaign.
His priority is to build his physical strength as he looks to accumulate Olympic qualifying points in the 65kg category after the 60kg class, his main event, was dropped from the LA28 programme.
The Segamat-born lifter competed in the 61kg category at the 2024 Paris Olympics, where he missed out on bronze by one kilogramme.
The category has now been increased to 65kg.
Aniq said he was still adapting to the new category, with a particular focus on building strength and muscle.

"My preparations now are mainly focused on qualifying for the Olympics. I am now focusing on the World Championships and the IWF qualifier," said Aniq, who participated in the Oxyenergy Media Prima Merdeka Run at Balai Berita here today.
"The 60kg category is no longer available, so I have to move up to 65kg.
"At the moment, I am still in the process of adapting because I have only recently moved up to the 65kg category. Frankly, the lifts are not there yet."
On his chances of qualifying for LA28, the 24-year-old admitted that the road would not be easy.

While Paris qualification was based on the top eight in the world rankings, with each lifter's best lift taken into consideration, the current qualifying process features 10 events, with a lifter's best five results used to determine the eight qualifiers.
"There are many Olympic qualifying events. Next year alone, there are five," he added.
Five Olympic qualifying events will be held next year, with the remaining three in 2028.
Aniq, however, will be aiming to record his best lifts early to ensure he does not miss out on qualification for LA28.
Three-time Commonwealth Games champion Aznil Bidin, who also participated in the fun run, will compete in the same weight category in the Olympic qualifiers.
However, Aznil has skipped the World Championships and will travel to Doha for the qualifier to begin his Olympic quest.

3e799e56f038113f: KANGAR, Sept 13 — The body of a fisherman who fell into the sea while fishing near Pulau Batu Layang, Sungai Baru here yesterday, was found about 400 metres from the island today.
The victim was identified as Khairul Amir Bahroom, 33, who was reported missing at about 3.30 am yesterday while out at sea with his elder brother.

Kuala Perlis Maritime Zone director Maritime Commander Nak Rong A/L Si Prom said the body was discovered by local fishermen and the finding was reported to the search and rescue operation team this morning.
“The operation team received information from the fishing community about the discovery of a body approximately 400 metres from Pulau Batu Layang,” he said in a statement today.
He said Bot Benteng 1207 subsequently retrieved the body and brought it to the Kuala Perlis Customs Jetty before handing it over to police for further action.
Kangar District Police Chief ACP Yusharifuddin Mohd Yusop confirmed that the body would be taken to the Forensic Unit of Hospital Tuanku Fauziah (HTF) for a post-mortem. — Bernama
4b1926374344a4d1: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is constantly planning and projecting healthcare service requirements to prepare for a possible increase in the number of patients at public hospitals amid rising health insurance costs.

Director-General of Health Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab said such planning and projections formed part of the public healthcare sector’s day-to-day and long-term planning, including financial requirements to meet changes in demand for healthcare services.
“In the healthcare sector, particularly the public sector, we make projections as part of our day-to-day and long-term planning to anticipate what may happen and so on.

“These projections form one of the bases for planning and government financial support to ensure healthcare service needs can be met,” he told reporters after officiating the Malaysian Trauma Conference (MTC) 2026 here today.

He was responding to reports quoting KSI Strategic Institute for Asia Pacific president Tan Sri Michael Yeoh as saying that health insurance costs, which have risen by up to 20 per cent annually, were becoming increasingly worrying and required serious attention to prevent the financial burden on the public from worsening.

Dr Mahathar said the ministry was also aware of concerns over reported increases of up to 20 per cent annually in health insurance costs, which could place a greater financial burden on the public and affect demand for public healthcare services.

He said MOH and the Ministry of Finance (MOF) were working together through a joint committee to look into the issue, including the government’s Medi-Asas programme, an insurance and takaful medical protection plan designed to provide Malaysians with access to more affordable and sustainable health coverage.
“As for insurance and related matters, these fall more under the purview of other agency that regulate aspects such as premiums,” he said. — Bernama
126d5fac74edf604: PETALING JAYA: From the internet and webcams to artificial hearts and mRNA vaccines, university research has helped shape technologies that have changed how people live.
But taking a discovery from the laboratory to the market requires more than a promising idea. It needs funding, industry expertise and a clear understanding of the market it is intended to serve.

The University Research and Innovation Investment Summit (URIIS) 2026 aims to bridge the gap by bringing together all 20 public universities, investors and businesses to explore how Malaysian research can be translated into market-ready solutions.

Jointly organised by the higher education ministry and Universiti Putra Malaysia (UPM), the summit will take place from Sept 21-23 at World Trade Centre Kuala Lumpur and highlight more than 200 technologies with investment potential.
For researchers, it offers a chance to take their work beyond academic circles, while businesses and investors can explore technologies and partnerships that could meet their needs.
Making research ready for investment
For research to attract investment, potential investors need to understand the problem it solves, the demand for it and whether it can be produced or delivered at a scale that makes commercial sense.
Meanwhile, industry partners can also help researchers understand practical requirements, from production costs and regulatory considerations to how a solution would fit into existing operations.

URIIS aims to create space for these conversations, connecting research teams with investors and industry players who can assess their ideas, provide market feedback and identify possible pathways towards commercialisation.
Its scheduled programme includes pitching arenas for investment and commercialisation, alongside dedicated sessions for research and industry feedback.

A Cradle grant pitching clinic, an intellectual property commercialisation masterclass by Malaysian Research Accelerator for Technology and Innovation (MRANTI), and market-readiness sessions are also scheduled to help participants prepare for that journey.
Opportunities across 12 niche clusters
The summit covers 12 niche clusters, reflecting opportunities across technology, healthcare, energy, food security, and other areas with commercial and societal potential.

These include semiconductors, nanotechnology and advanced materials; digital finance and business technology; agricultural technology and food biotechnology; and life sciences, health technology and pharmaceuticals.
Other areas span sustainable energy, advanced manufacturing, artificial intelligence and robotics, alongside halal technology, education, smart cities, defence, aerospace and transportation.
The summit will also explore biodiversity, ecotourism, indigenous knowledge and national heritage, highlighting the broader economic and societal potential of Malaysian research.
Turning challenges into opportunities
The programme links research and innovation to real-world challenges, including early health monitoring for an ageing population, poultry health and predictive maintenance in industry.
For universities, stronger industry relationships can open opportunities for technology transfer, collaborative research, commercialisation and new sources of funding.
Companies, in turn, can gain access to emerging technologies and talent, potentially helping them improve productivity or develop new products and services.

Successful commercialisation could also support the creation of new businesses, skilled jobs and export opportunities, giving Malaysia greater economic and societal returns from its research capabilities.
Want to see how Malaysian research and innovation can translate into real investment and commercial opportunities?
Join URIIS 2026 and be part of the journey from research to market.
6b6471a2c2bbf012: BATU PAHAT: More than 600 vape cartridges containing liquid suspected to be drugs known as "Piu Piu", worth an estimated RM160,000, were seized after a suspect fled in a boat during a maritime patrol in Senggarang here, last week.
The suspect fled in a fibre boat when he spotted the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA) patrol boat on Sept 5.
It is believed that the suspect was about to pick up the "Piu-Piu" consignment hidden along shore.

"Piu Piu" is a street term used for synthetic cannabinoid-containing vape liquid. Its effects can include euphoria, confusion, hallucinations, severe anxiety, impaired coordination and, in some cases, seizures or loss of consciousness.
MMEA Batu Pahat Zone director Maritime Commander Mohammad Zaini Zainal said the patrol team spotted the fibre boat behaving suspiciously while conducting surveillance in the waters off Senggarang.
"Upon noticing the presence of the enforcement patrol boat, the suspect on board fled in the fibre boat.

"Further inspection along the shore line, enforcement officers found a black bag containing more than 600 vape cartridges filled with liquid suspected to contain the drug known as 'Piu Piu'," he told the New Straits Times, today.
The seizure was estimated to be worth RM160,000.
The seized cartridges were brought to the Batu Pahat Maritime Zone office for further investigation, while samples of the vape liquid were sent for laboratory analysis to confirm their contents.
Maritim Malaysia is investigating the case and has urged members of the public and the maritime community to channel information on suspicious activities in the country's waters to the authorities.
aafdad9bf12c2470: KUALA LUMPUR: The Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Tabung Haji (TH) has drawn widespread attention, particularly as the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is also investigating related issues involving charges against prominent individuals.

The question is to what extent the investigation can shed light on issues surrounding management, investment decisions and possible leakages or abuse of power that may have affected depositors' interests.
Harian Metro reporter Muhaamad Hafis Nawawi spoke to MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman for his views on the matter.

Question: The MACC's arrest of several individuals, including TH's top management, has fuelled perceptions that there were orders from 'above' and that the arrests were politically motivated. What is your comment on this?
Answer: I would like to stress that the MACC's position is clear, we will continue to conduct investigations fairly, transparently and courageously, regardless of anyone's position or influence.
The principle is simple: investigate without fear or favour. This remains the MACC's guiding principle to ensure every investigation is carried out professionally, without pressure or fear.
This is to safeguard the integrity, image and credibility of the MACC as the country's anti-corruption enforcement agency, while also ensuring public confidence in the institution is not eroded.
Every investigation is conducted fairly and transparently, without favouring any party involved, to safeguard the integrity of the organisation.

As is known, the RCI report was completed some time ago and only recently made public. The MACC had also conducted investigations into the matter previously, so why are there large-scale arrests only now? Was there insufficient evidence previously and has new evidence since emerged?
The MACC's detention of several prominent individuals and VVIPs following the disclosure of the RCI report on the TH Board was not conducted arbitrarily or based solely on old cases.
In fact, a committee was appointed not only to examine the report but also previous investigations conducted by the MACC into issues involving TH.

The appointed investigating officers were instructed to investigate based solely on complaints and information received and to do so in accordance with established standard operating procedures (SOPs).
At the MACC, I established a committee to review new investigation papers (IPs), as well as old investigation papers for which no decision has yet been made.
Some investigation papers had been opened previously but remained pending, with no decision made.

This committee will screen and examine the status of these old investigation papers, including those for which no decision has been reached. A decision will then be made on whether they should be reopened.
QUESION: What is the current status of the investigation into the TH RCI issues, and what about the charges?

ANSWER: As I mentioned, the MACC established a special task force on July 31 to review and examine the findings of the TH RCI. It is headed by MACC investigation division senior director Datuk Mohd Hafaz Nazar. The investigation focuses on the MACC Act 2009 (Act 694) and the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613).
At the initial stage of the investigation, six issues raised in the RCI report were examined:
- allegations of corruption in the purchase of Ladang Weida (M) Berhad by TH Plantation, a subsidiary of the Lembaga Tabung Haji;
- allegations of misappropriation and abuse of power involving the rental of Restoran Opah at KL Sentral;
- allegations of misappropriation and abuse of power involving the rental of Restoran Nasi Dalca on the second floor of the LTH headquarters;
- allegations of misconduct and corruption by a former LTH chief operating officer involving renovations to a house and office;
- allegations of document forgery involving the supply of rubber seedlings by TH Plantation at Ladang TH-Usia Jatimas in Sandakan; and
- allegations of misconduct and misappropriation involving officers of THP Bina Sdn Bhd and THP Timur Sdn Bhd, both subsidiaries of TH Properties Sdn Bhd.
From these six initial issues, six investigation papers were opened, with several actions taken, including arrests, remand applications, witness statements and searches of the premises involved.
Seven individuals were arrested in connection with the investigations, while 115 witnesses were called to assist in the cases.
All six investigation papers have been completed and submitted to the deputy public prosecutor (DPP) for review on Aug 21 and 28. Of these, two resulted in charges being brought.
For the remaining four investigation papers, no charges were recommended and they were classified as no further action (NFA).
Apart from the six issues raised in the RCI report, the special task force also examined eight other issues that had been identified.
Eight investigation papers were opened on Aug 10, most of which involved problematic investment issues, and these investigations are still ongoing.
Of the eight investigation papers opened, 11 people have been detained, including a former minister.
Overall, the RCI Investigation Special Task Force has opened 14 investigation papers.
A total of 18 individuals have been arrested, while 11 have been remanded, with 245 witnesses called to facilitate in the investigations.
The MACC has also come under fire over this issue, with claims that it is being used as a political tool. How does the MACC respond to such perceptions?
The investigations are still ongoing and I urge all parties to give the MACC the space and support to carry out these investigations independently and fairly.
For now, we will see whether the committee appointed recommends further action, including charges in court. If there are no charges, then there will be none.
I reiterate that the MACC's position is clear: we conduct investigations without being influenced by any party and are not a political tool.
We conduct investigations fairly, transparently and courageously, without fear or favour, to ensure every investigation is carried out professionally and without pressure or fear.

QUESTION: The issue of remand and the use of orange clothing has been widely discussed following the arrests of several VVIPs, including a minister, in connection with the TH issue. The prime minister has also called for the practice to be stopped. Could you comment on this?

ANSWER: As everyone is aware, the MACC has heeded the prime minister's advice and has also suspended, with immediate effect, the use of orange clothing for persons under investigation brought to court for remand applications.
I would also like to stress that the immediate suspension applies to everyone, regardless of the individual's status.
The rule applies to everyone, including politicians, regardless of their status.
Persons under investigation can wear their own clothes when brought to court, while lock-up clothing will only be worn while they are detained in the lock-up.
As for the use of handcuffs, this will depend on certain circumstances, with exemptions for persons under investigation who are infirm, persons with disabilities, children and senior citizens.
The MACC will continue to take precautionary measures by ensuring appropriate security controls are in place throughout the handling of persons under investigation.

We also remain committed to ensuring that every action taken in handling persons under investigation is carried out professionally, with integrity and prudence, and in accordance with the law and established procedures.

2a5651fed8412c9e: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that Malaysia is exploring the possibility of acquiring India’s BrahMos air-to-surface missile system, while emphasising that discussions are still ongoing and no final decision has been made.

In an interview with India’s NDTV, he said discussion on it took place during the bilateral meeting with his Indian counterpart, Narendra Modi, but the rightful decision maker would be Malaysia’s Air Force.
“(We) did discuss, but normally my position is always to get the departments or agencies concerned, those having the expertise in the Air Force, they should then continue.
“They have had initial discussions and I told Prime Minister Modi that I am very supportive of that because this relationship is build on trust and we want to cement it in all fields,” he said.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, acknowledged India’s defence capabilities.
The BrahMos is a long-range, ramjet-powered supersonic cruise missile that can be launched from submarines, ships, fighter aircraft or transporter erector launcher.
It is a joint venture between India’s Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) and the Russian Federation’s NPO Mashinostroyeniya, who together formed BrahMos Aerospace. — Bernama
2fd1c80bc9d3049c: JAKARTA: Operasi mencari dan menyelamat (SAR) dilancarkan selepas kapal penumpang, Virgo Transport 8 yang membawa 243 penumpang serta anak kapal dilaporkan hilang di Laut Jawa, Indonesia pada awal Ahad, ketika dalam pelayaran dari Surabaya di Jawa Timur ke Banjarmasin di Kalimantan Selatan.

Ketua Pejabat SAR Banjarmasin I, Putu Sudayana, berkata pihaknya menerima makluman kehilangan kapal itu pada 4.10 pagi selepas terputus hubungan komunikasi kira-kira 2 pagi ketika cuaca buruk di Laut Jawa.
"Kami menerima laporan terputus hubungan dengan kapal itu dan segera mengerahkan anggota serta sebuah kapal pencarian ke arah anggaran posisi terakhirnya," katanya dalam kenyataan.
Putu berkata, kapal itu berlepas dari Surabaya pada Sabtu dan kali terakhir diketahui berada kira-kira 80 batu nautika dari pangkalan SAR di Banjarmasin.

Beliau menggesa keluarga penumpang, kru kapal itu dan orang ramai kekal tenang.
ad69b60aba84e7d3: SAPTARI, Nepal: For 10 days, Nepali hydropower worker Sanjay Sah survived in darkness inside a flooded tunnel, drinking muddy water and losing all sense of time as he desperately prayed for rescue.
When a disaster response team finally pulled him to safety on September 4, Sah's first question showed how deeply the ordeal had disoriented him.
"When I was rescued I first asked, how many days has it been?" Sah, 30, told AFP in an interview, while on his way back home in Saptari district Sunday.
"He said that it has been 10 days. I thought it had been just a few days."
Sah was among hundreds of workers at a series of hydropower projects hit by the catastrophic August 26 flood, triggered by a glacial mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border.
Sah's extraordinary survival was a rare ray of hope after a disaster that killed at least 1,429 people and left more than 5,640 missing, the majority in Nepal.
Struggling to hold back tears as friends and family welcomed him with garlands and a cake, Sah recalled how the disaster struck with stunning speed.
"I was on duty, and then suddenly an unthinkable flood hit us, with tsunami-like waves that were several metres tall," he said.
Workers had received warnings that floodwaters were approaching, but did not get enough time to escape, he said.
"We did get information to stay alert, that a big flood is coming. As much as possible, we tried to be alert and evacuate our friends," Sah said.
"But the water did not give us much time... we shut down everything, and tried to rescue and evacuate our friends."
Within minutes, however, the tunnel was engulfed by raging waters.
The sheer scale of the flood was unlike anything witnesses had seen before, with the government pointing the finger at the dire impact of rising global temperatures on Nepal's Himalayan mountains.
'Divine energy'
Separated from his colleagues, Sah found himself stranded with little idea whether anyone would ever reach him.
His Hindu faith helped carry him through the days of darkness and isolation.
"I survived because of my deep belief and confidence," he said.
"I was chanting Maha Mantra (Hindu prayers), and the divine energy I received because of that allowed me to not be scared or despair," he said.
"I was able to stay there."
With no clean water to drink, he survived on whatever he could find.
"There was water, but it was muddy," he said. "I only had that."
The darkness and isolation might have been overwhelming, but Sah was not entirely alone.
Another trapped worker, Kabir Maharjan, 45, had survived nearby.
"We were separated but speaking to each other."
The ability to hear another human voice offered a lifeline to Sah.
Eventually, after days of excavation and painstaking rescue efforts, search teams broke through to the trapped men and brought them out alive.
Sah's wife, Lakshmi Kumari Sah, said she never gave up hope of seeing her husband again.
"God has helped us, we had our hopes," she said, holding her daughter in her arms.
Sah, who spent several days recuperating in a Kathmandu hospital, says he has mixed emotions.
"I am happy, but I feel sad too," he said. "I was able to get a second life, to survive there. But many of our friends were there."
As rescuers continue searching through the tunnels, Sah urged authorities not to abandon the effort.
One Chinese worker was rescued on September 5, the day after Sah – but no signs of life have been heard since.
"I hope the government continues its search and rescue. It is possible there might still be someone alive," he said.
"Or they will be able to find bodies of friends who have passed away and hand them over to their families." — AFP

0ac1ae606ba8a753: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit is expected to trade within a tight range against the US dollar next week, with investors remaining cautious ahead of key monetary policy decisions by the United States Federal Reserve (Fed) and the Bank of Japan (BOJ).

Bank Muamalat Malaysia Bhd chief economist Dr Mohd Afzanizam Abdul Rashid said the focus next week will be on the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) and BOJ monetary policy meetings. Both central banks are expected to raise their respective policy rates by 25 basis points.

Market participants will also monitor the Fed's latest economic projections closely for gross domestic product (GDP) growth, inflation, the unemployment rate and the federal funds rate, he told Bernama.
"Expectations of a rate hike by the US Fed have shaped sentiment in the foreign exchange market, lending support to the US dollar," he said.
Against this backdrop, Mohd Afzanizam said the ringgit is likely to remain within a tight range of between RM4.06 and RM4.08 against the US dollar next week.
He also said external developments, particularly the sharp rise in crude oil prices amid the intensifying US-Israel-Iran conflict, are also expected to influence market sentiment.
"The escalation has pushed Brent crude oil prices higher to around US$104.64 per barrel," he said.
Meanwhile, on a Friday-to-Friday basis, the ringgit weakened against the greenback to 4.0685/0725 from 4.0425/0465 a week earlier.
The local currency traded lower against a basket of major currencies during the week.

The ringgit depreciated against the British pound to 5.4961/5015 from 5.4663/4717 last Friday, fell against the Japanese yen to 2.6400/6428 from 2.5832/5860, and declined against the euro to 4.7178/7225 from 4.6962/7008.
It also traded lower against ASEAN currencies.
The local note weakened against the Singapore dollar to 3.2091/2125 from 3.1888/1923 a week earlier and depreciated against the Thai baht to 12.3072/3241 from 12.2693/2863.
It also declined against the Indonesian rupiah to 231.0/231.3 from 229.1/229.4 and eased against the Philippine peso to 6.49/6.50 from 6.45/6.46 last Friday.
9b470fd0c7ba5aa5: PETALING JAYA: Pertemuan pimpinan PAS dan Umno Kedah tidak lama lagi sekadar perbincangan santai mengenai perkembangan politik semasa, kata Menteri Besar Kedah, Sanusi Nor.
Pengarah pilihan raya PAS itu berkata, sebarang keputusan berkaitan pengagihan kerusi tertakluk kepada PAS Pusat dan Perikatan Nasional (PN) sepenuhnya.

"Perjumpaan (dengan Umno Kedah) setakat sembang tentang perkembangan semasa parti masing-masing sahaja. Soal kerusi ini hanya boleh diputuskan PAS Pusat selepas berunding di peringkat nasional, bukan di peringkat negeri," katanya kepada FMT.

Semalam, Sanusi mengesahkan beliau akan menemui Ketua Umno Kedah, Mahdzir Khalid dan bekas menteri besar Kedah, Ahmad Bashah Md Hanipah bagi meneroka kemungkinan kerjasama politik antara dua parti di negeri itu.

Setakat ini, katanya, beliau difahamkan soal agihan kerusi berdasarkan status quo atau keadaan sedia ada, namun Umno-Barisan Nasional (BN) boleh meneroka kawasan hendak ditandingi jika mereka belum memiliki sebarang kerusi seperti di Kedah.
Sebelum ini, Umno Kedah menyuarakan kesediaan mengadakan perbincangan kerjasama politik dengan PAS negeri, namun menegaskan rundingan itu tidak akan melibatkan parti komponen PN yang lain.
Sanusi menepis kebimbangan parti komponen lain akan berasa terabai kerana sebarang perkembangan pertemuan itu akan disalurkan kepada pimpinan tertinggi.
"Tak ada kebimbangan itu kerana apa sahaja perkembangan akan dibawa kepada PAS Pusat dan mesyuarat PN."
Sementara itu, Ketua Pemuda Gerakan, Wong Chia Zhen, berkata sebarang bentuk kerjasama politik mesti berteraskan keikhlasan serta kehendak rakyat, bukan sekadar platform untuk kembali berkuasa.
Menurutnya, parti itu kekal konsisten mempertahankan prinsip keharmonian dan ketelusan dalam pembentukan jajaran politik.

4b5ace57fd895ef6: SAPTARI Sept 13 — For 10 days, Nepali hydropower worker Sanjay Sah survived in darkness inside a flooded tunnel, drinking muddy water and losing all sense of time as he desperately prayed for rescue.
When a disaster response team finally pulled him to safety on September 4, Sah’s first question showed how deeply the ordeal had disoriented him.
“When I was rescued I first asked, how many days has it been?” Sah, 30, told AFP in an interview, while on his way back home in Saptari district Sunday.
“He said that it has been 10 days. I thought it had been just a few days.”
Sah was among hundreds of workers at a series of hydropower projects hit by the catastrophic August 26 flood, triggered by a glacial mountain collapse on the China-Nepal border.
Sah’s extraordinary survival was a rare ray of hope after a disaster that killed at least 1,429 people and left more than 5,640 missing, the majority in Nepal.
Struggling to hold back tears as friends and family welcomed him with garlands and a cake, Sah recalled how the disaster struck with stunning speed.
“I was on duty, and then suddenly an unthinkable flood hit us, with tsunami-like waves that were several metres tall,” he said.
Workers had received warnings that floodwaters were approaching, but did not get enough time to escape, he said.
“We did get information to stay alert, that a big flood is coming. As much as possible, we tried to be alert and evacuate our friends,” Sah said.
“But the water did not give us much time... we shut down everything, and tried to rescue and evacuate our friends.”
Within minutes, however, the tunnel was engulfed by raging waters.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Nepali soldiers spend days of digging inside the Chilime Hydropower Station days for survivors after deadly flash floods and mudslides in Nepal's Rasuwa district on September 10, 2026. — AFP pic
The sheer scale of the flood was unlike anything witnesses had seen before, with the government pointing the finger at the dire impact of rising global temperatures on Nepal’s Himalayan mountains.
‘Divine energy’
Separated from his colleagues, Sah found himself stranded with little idea whether anyone would ever reach him.
His Hindu faith helped carry him through the days of darkness and isolation.
“I survived because of my deep belief and confidence,” he said.
“I was chanting Maha Mantra (Hindu prayers), and the divine energy I received because of that allowed me to not be scared or despair,” he said.
“I was able to stay there.”
With no clean water to drink, he survived on whatever he could find.
“There was water, but it was muddy,” he said. “I only had that.”
The darkness and isolation might have been overwhelming, but Sah was not entirely alone.
Another trapped worker, Kabir Maharjan, 45, had survived nearby.
“We were separated but speaking to each other.”
The ability to hear another human voice offered a lifeline to Sah.
Eventually, after days of excavation and painstaking rescue efforts, search teams broke through to the trapped men and brought them out alive.
Sah’s wife, Lakshmi Kumari Sah, said she never gave up hope of seeing her husband again.
“God has helped us, we had our hopes,” she said, holding her daughter in her arms.
Sah, who spent several days recuperating in a Kathmandu hospital, says he has mixed emotions.
“I am happy, but I feel sad too,” he said. “I was able to get a second life, to survive there. But many of our friends were there.”
As rescuers continue searching through the tunnels, Sah urged authorities not to abandon the effort.
One Chinese worker was rescued on September 5, the day after Sah — but no signs of life have been heard since.
“I hope the government continues its search and rescue. It is possible there might still be someone alive,” he said.
“Or they will be able to find bodies of friends who have passed away and hand them over to their families.” — AFP

b730a5b854380f44: MARAWI: Near a resettlement site for survivors of the bloody 2017 siege of Marawi, a woman wearing a black face veil walks across a hilltop dotted by tombstones without names.
Sophia Aminolla, a nurse and mother of two, does not know if her missing younger brother Amerel is among those lying beneath the numbered graves. She is not alone.

As the now semi-autonomous Muslim region in the southern Philippines aims to turn a new page with its first elections on Monday, the gravesite is a painful reminder that the healing is far from complete.
"I don't know if he is still alive or not. But my instinct says he's alive, because he always comes home in my dreams," Aminolla told AFP during a visit to the site this week.

From May to October of 2017, the Philippine military and gunmen linked to the Islamic State group fought brutal house-to-house battles that turned Marawi's 400-hectare business district into a ghost town.
More than a thousand people were killed by official count, mostly civilians. The number of missing varies, with the International Committee of the Red Cross listing more than 300 individuals.

"What the siege destroyed is not only the physical structures, the dead, but the social fabric of our community," Drieza Lininding, chairman of local rights monitor Moro Consensus Group, told AFP at the gravesite, where as many as six bodies are contained in some plots.
The displaced, along with relatives of those killed, are eligible for compensation.
A special government board has been created to handle their claims, with about 6.5 billion pesos (US$104 million) paid out so far, and at least half of the estimated 14,000 claimants still waiting.
But the board requires a death certificate issued by the government for "presumptive deaths", Marawi Compensation Board spokesman Johary Lumna said.
Aminolla, who now leads an advocacy group for the war missing, said her family's claim had been rejected.
A relative spotted her brother last at a hospital in a nearby town where he was taken after being injured by an explosion, she said.
He was never seen again.
- 'GROUND ZERO' -
At Marawi's "ground zero", faint construction sounds can now be heard as a few of the darkened hulls of destroyed buildings are rebuilt with help from indemnities.
Teenage girls in headscarves zoom across the nearby lakefront on e-scooters as children play next to picnicking mothers.

Majul Gandamra, mayor during the Marawi battle, estimates around 10 per cent of the city's 2017 population of about 200,000 have yet to return or be resettled, even as business now booms at the city's new commercial district.

Soraya Tambo, 73, has reopened her motorcycle parts shop on the ground floor of her four-storey property, aided by 500,000 pesos in building materials and some cash handed out by the regional government.
The empty upper floors still bear the scars of war she hopes to fix when her pending compensation claim comes through.
On one wall, colourful graffiti left behind by combatants from the IS-aligned Maute group reads: "End War!"
- EMPTY SHELVES -
Four kilometres away, displaced families at the temporary Sagonsongan resettlement site still live inside cramped 16 square-metre units they were supposed to have vacated in 2022.
Mother of six Annalyn Pangandaman, 47, said there is no tap water and the community endures intermittent power cuts. Her husband Jamil, 50, has struggled to land steady work.
"I'm a grocer, but my shelves are empty, zero. We have eaten everything," she told AFP.
Still traumatised by the fighting, her now 12-year-old daughter will cry and jump into their arms at "the mere sound of something falling on the floor", she added.

"Maybe the greatest injustice that these folks have faced since they lost their homes originally (is) their inability to return," Acram Latiph, executive director of the Institute for Peace and Development in Mindanao, told AFP.
With its mandate set to expire in 2028, time is running out for the compensation board to handle the thousands of cases still in process.
For others, like Aminolla, money will never be the answer.
"We're angry because we are not being given the right answers," she said of her missing brother.
"Why is the government still sleeping?"--AFP

146baf331716e01c: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) aims to develop a more integrated national trauma network to ensure patients receive the right care, at the right place and at the right time, regardless of where they are in Malaysia.

Director-General of Health Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab said the initiative was important to ensure a more interconnected trauma care system while narrowing access gaps between urban and rural areas, as well as Sabah and Sarawak.

He said the trauma chain of survival must be strengthened comprehensively, from bystander response and first aid at the scene to pre-hospital emergency medical services and transportation, resuscitation at the Emergency Department, definitive trauma care and rehabilitation.

“The chain is only as strong as its weakest link. We need seamless coordination across all these stages, with the right skills, adequate resources and the right system working together as one continuum of care,” he said when launching the Malaysian Trauma Conference (MTC) 2026 here today.
He said access to quality trauma care should not depend on a patient’s location, as every Malaysian deserved timely and appropriate trauma care.
Meanwhile, he said up to 30 per cent of trauma deaths were considered preventable based on the first National Trauma Registry report published in 2008.

Dr Mahathar, who was among the report’s co-authors, said the situation highlighted the need for a comprehensive transformation of the country’s trauma care system, stressing that “in trauma, every second, every minute counts”.

He said trauma remained a major public health challenge, particularly among the younger and working-age population, with transport-related injuries continuing to be a major contributor to preventable deaths.

He added that trauma care was also becoming increasingly complex as Malaysia moved towards an ageing population, with more patients presenting with multiple non-communicable diseases (NCDs) such as diabetes, hypertension and cardiovascular disease.
“These NCDs significantly influence how patients respond to trauma, how quickly they deteriorate and how they recover. Therefore, we can no longer look at trauma care in isolation,” he said.

Dr Mahathar said the National Trauma Transformation Conference Roadshow (NTTR) 2025-2026, involving six locations across Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak, was implemented to address these challenges systematically by aligning local clinical practices with global benchmarks, sharing best practices and promoting continuous quality improvement.
He stressed that MOH’s challenge now was not merely to produce policies and guidelines, but to translate them into effective and actionable implementation plans.

“Our challenge is not about producing policies and guidelines. Our challenge is translating policies and guidelines into actionable implementation plans. In trauma management, this is not an option,” he said.

He said strengthening trauma care also required a whole-of-society approach involving government agencies, the private sector, NGOs, academia and local communities, with the focus extending beyond treatment to injury prevention.

“This includes strengthening injury prevention, safety advocacy, public education and targeted interventions, particularly for road traffic and occupational injuries. Prevention must be an integral part of our national trauma strategy,” he said.

He added that the ultimate goal was to ensure that when a serious injury occurred, the system was ready, healthcare personnel were prepared, services were connected and patients received the care they needed without delay. — Bernama

4eb12fb934e1045f: SINGAPORE, Sept 13 — Researchers in Singapore are developing an artificial intelligence tool that could help policymakers estimate how people might respond to economic measures such as cash handouts before the policies are implemented.

The tool, developed by four researchers at Nanyang Technological University (NTU), is designed to predict whether people are likely to spend or save additional money, what they might spend it on and how different policy designs could affect the outcome, The Straits Times reported today.
The project is among 14 worldwide selected for funding by OpenAI from more than 400 submissions to a call for proposals launched in April.

The NTU team, led by Nanyang Business School Provost’s Chair Professor in Information Systems Hyeokkoo Eric Kwon, will receive US$100,000 (S$126,800 or RM407,000) to develop and test the unnamed tool over the next six months.
The system is trained using transaction data from more than one million users of a South Korean mobile budgeting app, covering spending, retailers and monthly income between 2023 and 2025.

The data was collected from bank notifications, messages and emails sent to users when transactions were made, with names and bank account numbers removed and spending amounts, income and purchase times grouped into broader ranges.
Kwon said the system uses only anonymised data, with safeguards intended to prevent individual users from being identified.

“There should never be a situation where the data can only be matched to one profile. Depending on the level of sensitivity of the data, a profile is sufficiently anonymised if a minimum of three, five or 10 users share those exact same characteristics,” he was quoted as saying.
The researchers will then use AI agents to simulate how households might respond to proposed government policies.

For example, if a government were to give every citizen S$100 in cash vouchers, the system would estimate how much additional spending the measure could generate, where the money might be spent and how the results could differ under another policy design.
Kwon said conventional economic simulations often rely on rules based on interviews and surveys, which may not fully reflect how people behave when they actually receive money.
“Qualitative interviews and surveys are conducted to set these rules, but there is often a gap between how people actually behave and how they respond in surveys,” he said.

The researchers plan to test the AI against real-world spending data from South Korea, including transactions recorded before and after two rounds of government cash handouts distributed in July and September 2025.
Recipients had to spend the handouts at eligible retailers by November 2025, giving the team data against which to compare the system’s predictions.
The researchers also aim to make the tool open-source and capable of being used with different populations by February 2027.
The system is intended to analyse other information, including interests and political views, to improve its predictions and provide an explanation for how it reaches its conclusions.
Half of the OpenAI funding will be provided in cash, while the remainder will come as credits for subscriptions to OpenAI’s AI models.

c96293bb5011fa54: CORON: The death toll from a Philippine ferry fire jumped to 76 on Saturday after the coast guard confirmed the discovery of 41 more bodies aboard the burnt-out vessel.
The remains will be transported to a port in Coron, Palawan, coast guard spokeswoman Commodore Noemie Cayabyab said in a statement.

AFP watched hours earlier as disaster agency workers carried coffins to a cemetery in the resort town, intended for the temporary burial of victims of the fire that tore through the M/V June Aster on Wednesday.
The first 30 bodies arrived by sea earlier on Saturday as forensic specialists began the painstaking process of identifying the remains.
The confirmed death toll now stands at 76, including five bodies recovered in the immediate wake of the incident. The ship sits grounded about 7.5km off the coast.
One-metre deep graves have been dug to hold the victims' remains until DNA testing is completed, Kristine Ablana, a tourism official serving as an official spokesperson, told reporters on Saturday.
Relatives will be brought to identify personal items that may have belonged to family members.
"Once someone is able to verify... that this photo or these belongings are indeed those of their relative, they will be asked to provide a DNA sample," Ablana said.
Thirty passengers, including two Chilean nationals, and 13 crew have been rescued, according to the coast guard. Around a dozen people are believed to remain unaccounted for.
- 'HAPPENED IN SECONDS' -
Cayabyab said in a radio interview that the fire had begun in the cargo hold, then tore through the ship within seconds.
"From the time that they heard the loud explosion, the appearance of smoke, and then fire. It spread very quickly," she said of survivors' accounts.
"Everything happened in seconds," she said, adding that those who made it off the ship had not even had time to put on life jackets.
Near the pier where the bodies were to be returned, an emotional Josenit Mayo, 40, told AFP her daughter had been aboard the ferry, returning from the capital Manila for a family visit.
"She told me 'Mom, I want to go home as I'm missing my siblings,'" Mayo said. "She insisted she was lonely."
Myra Cabilan told AFP she had flown to Coron to find her missing brother, 40-year-old Rammel Gonzaga, who had taken the ferry from Manila on a business trip with his brother-in-law.
"His wife had just given birth a month ago. He was so happy he was given a daughter," Cabilan said, fighting back tears.
"At dawn, I still believed he survived. But he's still missing. I have lost hope."
Hundreds of people desperate for news about the incident have taken to leaving comments on the Facebook page of a local mayor, searching for relatives, friends and even a dog.
The archipelago nation of 116 million has a long history of disasters involving the inter-island ferries that ply its seas.
Many rely on cheap and poorly regulated boats and ships for transport between the country's more than 7,000 islands, despite regular accidents.
In January, a triple-decker ferry carrying more than 340 people sank off the southern Philippines, killing at least 52 people.
On Thursday, the company that owns the M/V June Aster, Atienza Interisland Ferries Inc, said it was fully cooperating with the investigation.--AFP

3280083cdb6b1883: PETALING JAYA: A leatherback turtle was detected landing and laying 81 eggs at Rantau Abang beach in Dungun early this morning, according to the Terengganu fisheries department.
Its director, Pang Nyukang, said it was believed to be the same leatherback turtle that was recorded landing at the Pasir Putih beach in Marang on Sept 1, Bernama reported.

He said the leatherback, which is the world’s largest turtle species, was believed to have laid its eggs at the beach between 1.30am and 2.30am, with the nest discovered by a licensed turtle egg collector at 4am.
However, the mother turtle had returned to the sea after laying its eggs and was no longer at the site when the nest was discovered.

“The fisheries department does not rule out the possibility that the leatherback turtle that landed was the same mother that landed and laid eggs at Pasir Putih Beach about two weeks ago,” he said in a statement.
Pang said the tracks left by the leatherback turtle measured 2.20m, while the eggs measured 5cm in diameter.
He said the eggs will be sent for incubation at the fisheries department's Turtle Conservation Centre Hatchery in Rantau Abang.
“The eggs are expected to hatch within 50 to 70 days from today,” he said.
He akso said the mother turtle is expected to return to the Rantau Abang stretch of beach to lay eggs for the third time in about two weeks.
Bernama previously reported that a leatherback turtle landed at Pasir Putih Beach on the night of Sept 1 and laid 44 eggs.
Before that landing, the last recorded landing of a leatherback turtle on any Terengganu beach was in 2017.
0667b5dcbd3414b4: KUALA LUMPUR: Kerajaan menegaskan akan terus komited dalam usaha mendapatkan semula aset 1MDB menerusi langkah seperti kerjasama dan proses perundangan di beberapa negara, menurut Kementerian Kewangan (MoF).

f473a62c406ed7fe: MADRID, Sept 13 — Lando Norris produced a “masterpiece” on Saturday as he claimed pole position for McLaren with a stunning lap to beat championship leader Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes in a tense qualifying session for the Spanish Grand Prix.

World champion Norris, who had missed most of second practice on Friday due to an enforced gearbox change, topped the times in one minute and 31.824 seconds to beat the 20-year-old Italian by just 0.011 seconds.

Max Verstappen of Red Bull was third, 0.140 seconds adrift, ahead of Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc with George Russell sixth in the second Mercedes at the new ultra-demanding, high-risk hybrid Madring circuit.
“It was a masterpiece and one of the best laps of his life,” said McLaren team chief Andrea Stella after seeing Norris defy the odds on a track he had described as “like Monaco on steroids”.
Norris said: “I’m shocked and bit surprised, but my God it was probably one of the best laps I have ever done in my career so I’m very, very happy, very proud and very happy for the team.
“It was one of those laps where everything came together. I had a good idea of what I wanted to do, but it was whether my brain would let me do it on the last lap and everything worked perfectly.

“The adrenaline was high on the last lap. It is just one where you have got to relax, just let it all flow. It is so easy to get tense around here — there’s a lot of walls that come out at you pretty quickly!
“It was pretty much perfect bar the last corner when I thought I was in the wall and the boys would be repairing the car tonight! But I achieved it and put a big smile on my face.”
Antonelli, who leads Russell by 66 points in the championship and Norris, who is fourth, by 96, said: “I thought it was a good lap, but then this guy just snatched it away. Good job to them!
“On my side, it was a very intense qualifying — difficult to get the balance right with the track being so hot, but the lap was pretty clean.”
Verstappen said he was pleased with his session’s work on a track he had forecast to be extremely challenging.

“For us, it was a very good qualifying. For me, to be third is a great result. The car felt quite decent in qualifying and I could attack corners the way I liked so for us I think this qualifying was a good result.”
Oscar Piastri was seventh in the second McLaren ahead of Liam Lawson in the second Red Bull, Alpine’s Franco Colapinto and Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad.

Norris’s pole was his third this year and his 19th overall, giving him a great chance of a third win of the season on a barrier-lined circuit with few overtaking opportunities. He has won both times he has started on pole this season — in Hungary and the Netherlands.

It also endorsed his reputation as an expert on tight street tracks, having claimed his first pole at Sochi in Russia in 2021 and secured poles on similar tracks like the Hungaroring, Monaco, Zandvoort, Las Vegas and Singapore. — AFP

b344cb6daa6aff45: LONDON: The Odyssey has surpassed Jurassic World as the highest-grossing Universal Pictures film of all time just months after its release, PA Media/dpa reported.

The blockbuster, which was released on July 17, is an adaptation of Homer's ancient Greek epic and follows Matt Damon as Odysseus, the Greek king of Ithaca, on his perilous 10-year journey home after the Trojan War.
The film, which has received strong reviews from critics, has surpassed US$1.677 billion worldwide, beating 2015 adventure film Jurassic World to become Universal's biggest film to date.
Jurassic World, which stars Chris Pratt and Bryce Dallas Howard, grossed approximately US$1.671 billion globally during its theatrical run.
The Odyssey is expected to gross US$1.685 billion globally this weekend, making it the 12th highest-grossing film of all time and the third-biggest non-franchise title of all time.
It is the highest-grossing film of Christopher Nolan's career, having made more than US$1 billion at the global box office less than a month after its release.
The 56-year-old wrote and directed The Odyssey, which he also produced alongside his wife, Emma Thomas.
Donna Langley, chairman of NBCUniversal entertainment, said: "What Chris and Emma have created will go down as one of the most ambitious and brilliantly executed films in cinematic history.
"A generational event that galvanises moviegoing itself."

Oscar-winning filmmaker Nolan has directed blockbusters such as Tenet, Dunkirk, and Interstellar, as well as the 2012 Batman movie The Dark Knight Rises, which previously held the top spot as his biggest film.
The Odyssey is a three-hour epic which features a star-studded cast including Damon, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Charlize Theron, Lupita Nyong'o, as well as Tom Holland and Zendaya.
The blockbuster debuted at number one worldwide and remained in the top position for two consecutive weekends both domestically and internationally.
It recently returned to the top spot globally in its eighth weekend.
It is also one of three Universal films to have grossed one billion dollars globally this year, alongside The Super Mario Galaxy Movie and Michael.
The Odyssey had a reported production budget of US$250 million, excluding marketing costs, making it one of the most expensive films of Nolan's career.

0f0a7fca60bd6b88: KUALA LUMPUR: Quartz deposits along Sungai Pahang could be worth up to RM3,657 per tonne, offering a potentially valuable mineral resource for the state, according to a geologist.

From a geological standpoint, the extensive sand deposits along the river are attributed to the upper reaches of Sungai Pahang being rich in granite with high quartz content, according to Kosmo! Ahad.
The granite breaks down into hard, durable quartz grains that are carried downstream in large quantities, forming new sandbanks along the river.

Universiti Malaysia Pahang Al-Sultan Abdullah (UMPSA) Sustainable Mineral Resources and Recovery Technology Centre (SMaRRT Center) director Associate Professor Dr Mohd Yuhyi Mohd Tadza said quartz was produced through the decomposition of granite, resulting in quartz sand with commercial value.
"Rocks from hills and mountains upstream, already eroded, are carried by water into the river and deposited according to weight — the finer the particles, the further downstream they travel.
"Their value depends on the type of parent rock and the quality after undergoing certain processes," he said.
Quartz is an important industrial mineral because of its hardness, purity and ability to withstand high temperatures.
It is used in industries including semiconductors, glassmaking, electronics and precision instruments.

He said no detailed study had been conducted specifically on Sungai Pahang's quartz deposits to date, but the mineral was valuable and could represent a source of wealth for the state and the country.
The price of quartz sand varies according to its quality after processing, with premium grades reaching up to RM3,657 per tonne.
Yuhyi said the applications of quartz depended heavily on its quality and purity.
"For high-quality quartz, this material is used in many other things — in the semiconductor industry, making glass, watch lenses and so on.
"It also has many uses in making paint, paper, electronic goods and precision timekeeping devices," he said.
He added that if a detailed study confirmed the presence of high-quality quartz along Sungai Pahang, the mineral could be processed and sold at a significantly higher price.
Selling quartz sand without prior processing would be wasteful, he said, as it would command a far lower market value than processed material.
0de7cff577e2dd89: PETALING JAYA: There is no need for Terengganu to hold a state election at this time as the state government is stable and performing well, says PAS deputy president Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man.
Tuan Ibrahim said elections are not to be used as testing grounds, or a tool for measuring the sincerity of political cooperation.
“As long as there is no urgent need, the people should not be burdened with the political pressure and costs of facing a state election,” he said
He was responding to a proposal by Umno deputy president Mohamad Hasan for an election in PAS-led Terengganu as proof the Islamic party is sincere about Malay unity.
In a statement, Tuan Ibrahim said state elections should only be held when the current term had ended, or there was a compelling reason to do so.
He said it would be better to dissolve Parliament and seek a fresh national mandate instead, adding that Perikatan Nasional had instructed its election machinery to prepare for any eventuality.

At the Umno general assembly yesterday, Mohamad, better known as Tok Mat, said if Umno and PAS could agree on a formula for seat negotiations in Terengganu, a similar approach could be adopted for the next general election.
Umno was wiped out in the 2023 Terengganu state election, when it failed to win any of the 27 seats contested.
PN made a clean sweep of all 32 seats – PAS with 27 and Bersatu five – leaving Terengganu without an opposition for the first time.
Umno and PAS formed an electoral pact for last month's Negeri Sembilan state election, and won 26 of the 36 seats.
Barisan Nasional and PN seemed poised to continue their alliance in the coming Melaka polls.

However, this appeared to have reached an impasse after BN chairman Ahmad Zahid Hamdi said the coalition wanted to contest all the 21 seats it won in 2021, while PN contended that negotiations were still being held.
Melaka has 28 state seats. In 2021, Pakatan Harapan won five, and PN two.

Malaysia's labour market continued to show resilience, with the unemployment rate unchanged at 3.0 per cent for the fourth consecutive month in July.
The latest data also suggests that earlier signs of softening have dissipated following revisions to previous figures.
Labour demand also strengthened significantly in August, with job vacancies rising by 126,200 to 368,600 from 242,400 in July.

Meanwhile, it said a favourable monetary stance and resilient domestic demand would remain important buffers against external and geopolitical headwinds.
"At the same time, the electrical and electronics sector's shift towards advanced AI-related chips should support further high-skilled employment creation," it added.
826ecbd6d7fdc8ba: LONDON, Sept 13 —The Odyssey has surpassed Jurassic World as the highest-grossing Universal Pictures film of all time just months after its release, PA Media/dpa reported.

The blockbuster, which was released on July 17, is an adaptation of Homer’s ancient Greek epic and follows Matt Damon as Odysseus, the Greek king of Ithaca, on his perilous 10-year journey home after the Trojan War.
The film, which has received strong reviews from critics, has surpassed US$1.677 billion worldwide, beating 2015 adventure film Jurassic World to become Universal’s biggest film to date.
Jurassic World, which stars Chris Pratt and Bryce Dallas Howard, grossed approximately US$1.671 billion globally during its theatrical run.
The Odyssey is expected to gross US$1.685 billion globally this weekend, making it the 12th highest-grossing film of all time and the third-biggest non-franchise title of all time.
It is the highest-grossing film of Christopher Nolan’s career, having made more than US$1 billion at the global box office less than a month after its release.
The 56-year-old wrote and directed The Odyssey, which he also produced alongside his wife, Emma Thomas.
Donna Langley, chairman of NBCUniversal entertainment, said: “What Chris and Emma have created will go down as one of the most ambitious and brilliantly executed films in cinematic history.
“A generational event that galvanises moviegoing itself.”

Oscar-winning filmmaker Nolan has directed blockbusters such as Tenet, Dunkirk, and Interstellar, as well as the 2012 Batman movie The Dark Knight Rises, which previously held the top spot as his biggest film.
The Odyssey is a three-hour epic which features a star-studded cast including Damon, Anne Hathaway, Robert Pattinson, Charlize Theron, Lupita Nyong’o, as well as Tom Holland and Zendaya.
The blockbuster debuted at number one worldwide and remained in the top position for two consecutive weekends both domestically and internationally.
It recently returned to the top spot globally in its eighth weekend.
It is also one of three Universal films to have grossed one billion dollars globally this year, alongside The Super Mario Galaxy Movie and Michael.
The Odyssey had a reported production budget of US$250 million, excluding marketing costs, making it one of the most expensive films of Nolan’s career. — Bernama
e7b2964f5e25f1ea: KERALAM: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim's visit to Keralam is expected to open up opportunities for new areas of cooperation between Malaysia and southern India in various fields, including wellness tourism, education, trade and investment.

The Consul General of Malaysia to South India, K. Saravana Kumar, said Keralam has extensive expertise in Ayurveda, as well as approaches that integrate traditional medicine with modern medicine, or allopathy, which Malaysia could potentially explore to develop its wellness tourism sector.

"In addition, tourism is also an area with significant potential for further strengthening, given the substantial flow of tourists between Malaysia and southern India, particularly involving Keralam and Tamil Nadu.

"Tourism ties benefit both countries, but we see significant potential to further increase the number of tourists from southern India visiting Malaysia," he told Malaysian media ahead of the Prime Minister's visit here, which begins today.

After attending the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi, Anwar will continue his journey to Keralam and is scheduled to meet the Grand Mufti of India, Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad, at Jamia Markaz here to exchange views on community development, educational advancement and interfaith harmony.

Elaborating, Saravana Kumar said Anwar's maiden visit to Keralam as Prime Minister is also highly significant in strengthening Malaysia-India bilateral ties, particularly with the states in southern India.
He said the visit is also expected to inject fresh momentum into Malaysia's relations with southern India, while opening up opportunities to explore areas of cooperation that are of mutual interest.

According to him, the Keralam state government views the Prime Minister's presence as an important development, given that Malaysia is a significant bilateral partner of India, and has made extensive preparations to provide Anwar with the best possible welcome and hospitality as a state guest.

Saravana Kumar said Keralam, which is also renowned for its extraordinary natural beauty and cultural heritage, also has a reputation for sustainable development, clean energy and implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which could be among the areas for both sides to exchange expertise and experience.

He said the Prime Minister's visit to Calicut, also known as Kozhikode, will also focus on business engagement and meetings with prominent Indian industry players and corporate figures, which are expected to open up new opportunities for cooperation and investment.

He said Anwar is also scheduled to meet Keralam Chief Minister V. D. Satheesan and Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar tomorrow to discuss bilateral cooperation between Malaysia and Keralam in key sectors such as trade and investment, tourism, healthcare and education.
The Prime Minister arrived in New Delhi on Friday to attend the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

Modern diplomatic relations between Putrajaya and New Delhi were established in 1957, shortly after Malaysia gained independence, and India remains Malaysia's largest trading partner in South Asia, with bilateral trade reaching USD18.55 billion (RM79.33 billion) in 2025.

The working visit is expected to further strengthen the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between the two countries, while opening new opportunities to expand high-impact cooperation, particularly in the economic, trade and investment sectors, digital technology and education. — BERNAMA
f582bc46e40c2c54: IPOH: Presiden Terpilih Persatuan Perubatan Malaysia (MMA) Dr L Sivanaesan dilantik sebagai presiden baharu persatuan itu menggantikan Dr R Thirunavukarasu yang menamatkan penggalnya mulai hari ini.
Beliau pernah memegang jawatan pengerusi MMA Selangor, timbalan setiausaha kehormat MMA selama dua penggal serta pengerusi Bahagian Pengamal Perubatan Swasta Kebangsaan.

Dalam ucapan pada majlis makan malam Persatuan Perubatan Malaysia (MMA) 2026 malam tadi, Sivanaesan berkata, mengekalkan doktor dalam sistem kesihatan awam menjadi keutamaannya ketika negara berdepan peningkatan tuntutan perkhidmatan kesihatan dan keperluan tenaga kerja dalam sektor berkenaan.
“Untuk melatih seorang doktor mengambil masa bertahun-tahun dan memerlukan pelaburan yang besar.

“Apabila doktor berpengalaman meninggalkan sistem kesihatan awam, kita bukan sekadar kehilangan tenaga kerja, malah kehilangan petugas yang berpengalaman, kepakaran dan kesinambungan rawatan kepada pesakit,” katanya.

Sivanaesan berkata, untuk mengekalkan doktor tidak boleh ditangani hanya dengan menambah jumlah graduan perubatan, sebaliknya tumpuan perlu diberikan kepada kemajuan kerjaya, persekitaran kerja, pembangunan profesional serta prospek jangka panjang.
